questions.prompt: The soldiers, having dared to cross the river, rejoiced at the victory.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs, flūmen trānsīre ausī, dē victōriā gāvīsī sunt.

questions.prompt: Whoever has dared great things is often praised by the poets.
questions.answer: Quīcumque magna ausus est saepe ā poētīs laudātur.

questions.prompt: Having dared to speak the truth, the philosopher was condemned.
questions.answer: Vērum dīcere ausus, philosophus damnātus est.

questions.prompt: The general was accustomed to trust his most faithful centurions.
questions.answer: Imperātor fīdissimīs centuriōnibus fīdere solēbat.

questions.prompt: As we were wont, we returned to the city before dawn.
questions.answer: Ut solitī erāmus, ante aurōram in urbem revertimus.

questions.prompt: The priests are accustomed to swear by the sacred altars.
questions.answer: Sacerdōtēs per sānctās ārās jūrāre solent.

questions.prompt: Having lunched in the shade, the travelers were wont to sleep.
questions.answer: In umbrā prānsī, viātōrēs dormīre solēbant.

questions.prompt: Trusting in his own strength, the youth dared to climb the cliff.
questions.answer: Suīs vīribus fīsus, iuvenis scopulum ascendere ausus est.

questions.prompt: We do not trust those who have often sworn falsely.
questions.answer: Nōn fīdimus eīs quī saepe falsō jūrāvērunt.

questions.prompt: Having trusted the winds, the men set out from the shore.
questions.answer: Ventīs fīsī, virī ā lītore profectī sunt.

questions.prompt: The commander trusted the promise which the envoy had sworn.
questions.answer: Dux prōmissō, quod lēgātus jūrāverat, fīsus est.

questions.prompt: Having drunk the wine, the guests dared to sing boldly.
questions.answer: Vīnō pōtī, convīvae audācter cantāre ausī sunt.

questions.prompt: The boy, having grown up in the countryside, trusted no one in the city.
questions.answer: Puer, rūrī adultus, nēminī in urbe fīdēbat.

questions.prompt: Having sworn their loyalty, the soldiers returned to the camp.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs fidem jūrātī in castra revertērunt.

questions.prompt: Tired from the journey, we turned aside into a small inn.
questions.answer: Itinere fessī, in parvam tabernam dēvertimus.

questions.prompt: The victors, having dined, were wont to boast of their deeds.
questions.answer: Victōrēs, cēnātī, dē rēbus gestīs glōriārī solēbant.

questions.prompt: I rejoiced that my brother had dared to defend the truth.
questions.answer: Gāvīsus sum frātrem meum vērum dēfendere ausum esse.

questions.prompt: Whenever the leader returned, the people were accustomed to rejoice.
questions.answer: Quotiēns dux reverterat, populus gaudēre solēbat.

questions.prompt: The old woman, having sworn to speak the truth, rejoiced greatly.
questions.answer: Anus, vēra dīcere iūrāta, magnopere gāvīsa est.

questions.prompt: Having dined, the guests were accustomed to return home late at night.
questions.answer: Cēnātī, hospitēs domum nocte serā revertī solēbant.

questions.prompt: The boys who had grown up in the countryside did not dare to enter the city.
questions.answer: Puerī, quī rūre adultī erant, urbem intrāre nōn ausī sunt.

questions.prompt: We trust the leader who is accustomed to conquer his enemies.
questions.answer: Ducī, quī hostēs suōs vincere solet, fīdimus.

questions.prompt: Having lunched in the shade, the traveler dared to continue the journey.
questions.answer: In umbrā prānsus, viātor iter pergere ausus est.

questions.prompt: The soldiers, having drunk much water, rejoiced and turned aside to the camp.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs, multā aquā pōtī, gāvīsī sunt et ad castra dēvertērunt.

questions.prompt: The queen was wont to trust her most faithful maidservant.
questions.answer: Rēgīna ancillae fidēlissimae suae fīdere solēbat.

questions.prompt: Since the plan had pleased everyone, the joyful general returned to Rome.
questions.answer: Cōnsiliō omnibus placitō, imperātor laetus Rōmam revertit.

questions.prompt: The veterans, having sworn to obey, rejoiced that peace had at last been restored.
questions.answer: Veterānī, pārēre jūrātī, gāvīsī sunt pācem tandem redditam esse.

questions.prompt: Trusting in the gods, the priestess dared to enter the burning temple.
questions.answer: Deīs fīsa, sacerdōs templum ārdēns intrāre ausa est.

questions.prompt: The old men, having dined lavishly, were wont to turn aside into the garden.
questions.answer: Senēs, laute cēnātī, in hortum dēvertī solēbant.

questions.prompt: Having grown up among soldiers, the boy was not afraid to trust the sword.
questions.answer: Inter mīlitēs adultus, puer gladiō fīdere nōn timēbat.

questions.prompt: We rejoice that you have returned unharmed from so great a war.
questions.answer: Gaudēmus tē ex tantō bellō incolumem revertisse.

questions.prompt: Having drunk deeply, the guests were accustomed to praise the host's generosity.
questions.answer: Largē pōtī, convīvae hospitis līberālitātem laudāre solēbant.

questions.prompt: The plan pleased the consul, who dared to attack the enemy by night.
questions.answer: Cōnsulī placuit cōnsilium, quī hostem noctū oppugnāre ausus est.

questions.prompt: Having lunched beside the river, the weary soldiers trusted the guide and set out.
questions.answer: Ad flūmen prānsī, mīlitēs fessī ducī fīsī profectī sunt.
